children: is underwater in after-hours trading after the company issued downbeat guidance for next year as it faces a more challenging consumer environment and a lower active client starting point, both of which are expected to hinder revenue growth for fiscal year 2027.

The outlook was also impacted by a reduction in Fix volume due to a decision to adjust the timing of some shipments in Q4, which shifted Fix volume from the first quarter of 2027 into the fourth quarter of 2026, and an unintended change made to the post-checkout order in August that limited the number of clients eligible to request another shipment. This has been corrected and will not impact first-quarter 2027 results.
For the first quarter of 2027, Stitch Fix
expects net revenue to decline by 4.1% to 5.6%, translating to a range of $323M and $328M, with a $325.5M midpoint that is below $355.15M estimates.
Adjusted EBITDA is seen between $3M and $6M with a margin between 0.9% and 1.8%.

For FY27, net revenue is expected to be down 2.8% to up 0.9%, translating to a range of $1.31B to $1.36B versus $1.41B estimates.  Adjusted EBITDA is seen between $27M and $42M with a margin of 2.1% to 3.1%. Gross margin is expected to be between 43% and 44%.
For its fiscal fourth quarter, Stitch Fix
experienced a 1.4% decline in active clients while net revenue per active client increased 7.8% to $592. This contributed to a 4.2% increase in net revenue to $324.4M, in line with expectations.
Net loss narrowed significantly to $2.1M, or $(0.02) per share, from a loss of $(0.07) per share in the same quarter last year and a net loss margin of 0.6% from a loss of 2.8% a year ago.
Shares are down 17% in after-hours trading.

title: Stitch Fix sees soft consumer spending weighing on FY27 sales
